To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 7, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 9
Subject: Request for safety study and signal timing fixes at West 125 Street & Amsterdam Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to request a safety study at the junction of West 125 Street & Amsterdam Avenue and action on the roads you are responsible for.

Official records for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 show 172 crashes, including 79 injury crashes. Pedestrians injured: 26. Cyclists injured: 24. People killed: 0. This location is a city priority location. The yearly cost of the harm, using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), is $5.4 million. No safety project is recorded in the period.

We ask you to consider:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent 0.7 pedestrian injury crashes and $231,000 in harm per year. Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.
* longer yellow signal times, expected to prevent 4.3 injury crashes and $1,471,000 in harm per year, after checking on site for an entry on yellow or red.

Please assess feasibility, funding, and timing for these fixes on West 125 Street and Amsterdam Avenue.

Thank you for your work on street safety.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Dear colleagues at NYSDOT Region 11 and NYC DOT,

We are writing about the junction of Astoria Boulevard North & Hoyt Avenue North.

For the roads you are responsible for [NYSDOT Region 11: BKLYN/QUEENS EXP (I 278); NYC DOT: Astoria Boulevard North, Hoyt Avenue North], we ask you to carry out a safety study at this location and consider fixes.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 213 crashes, including 78 injury crashes. 7 pedestrians and 3 cyclists were reported injured, and 1 person was killed. This location is a New York City priority location. In the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of the harm is $5.3 million. No safety work is recorded in this period [last recorded project: Astoria Boulevard at 31st and 33rd Streets, 2015].

Two low-cost signal measures could help reduce injury crashes, subject to an on-site check:

- longer yellow signal times, where an entry on yellow or red must be checked on site. On this record it is estimated to prevent about 4.2 injury crashes per year (about $1,453,000 in harm avoided per year).
- reflective backplates on the traffic signals, where an entry on yellow or red must be checked on site. Estimated to prevent about 2.3 injury crashes per year (about $801,000 per year).

Where measured in this city, a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green) was linked to fewer pedestrian injuries: where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain. This also needs a site check for a turning movement.

Please advise on next steps.

Yours sincerely,
